nodes.name: Nitrate pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Amount of Co(NO3)2·6H2O was put into a muffle furnace and heated at 500°C for 2h with a rising rate of 1°C/min under air atmosphere. After being cooled to room temperature, the product was collected and grinded for a while, the final Co3O4 powder was obtained.
nodes.source_text: The Co3O4 precursor was prepared by a nitrate pyrolysis method. In brief, amount of Co(NO3)2·6H2O was put into a muffle furnace...

nodes.name: Phosphorization of Co3O4
nodes.procedure: The as prepared Co3O4 powders were mixed with NaH2PO2·H2O in a weight ratio of 1:10. Then the mixture was put into a crucible with a cover. The crucible was annealed in a tube furnace at 350°C for 2h with a rising rate of 2°C/min under inert gas atmosphere. After cooling to room temperature, the product was collected by water rinsing several times and vacuum dried at 60°C for 12h.

nodes.name: Co(OH)2 precipitation
nodes.procedure: 400 mg of Co(NO3)2·6H2O and 50 mg of Sodium citrate monohydrate were dissolved in 100 mL of deionized (DI) water with a rapid stirring for 4h. Afterward, the precipitation was washed by water for several times and vacuum dried at 60°C for 12h. The Co(OH)2 precursor was obtained after cooling to room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₂P/CoP displays biphasic structure with Co₂P (121), (201), (211) planes at 40.7°, 41.0°, 43.3° and CoP (011), (112), (211) planes at 31.6°, 46.2°, 48.1°; weight contents of Co₂P phase are 74.8%, 44.7%, 25.7% at 300, 350, 400°C annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1(b), a series of peaks at 2θ of 40.7°, 41.0°, and 43.3° appeared in Co₂P/CoP catalysts can be ascribed to Co₂P phase of (121), (201), and (211) planes, while the peaks at 31.6°, 46.2°, and 48.1° belong to (011), (112), and (211) planes of CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface areas are 31.5 m²/g for Co₂P/CoP, 30.2 m²/g for CoP, and 30.3 m²/g for Co₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1(c) shows the nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms results. The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface areas (SSA) are 31.5, 30.2, and 30.3 m²/g for Co₂P/CoP, CoP, and Co₂P, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₂P/CoP catalysts display interconnected nanoparticle structures with average particle size of ~50 nm and slight agglomeration compared to Co₃O₄ precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of Co₃O₄ precursors and Co₂P/CoP catalysts are shown in Figs. 2(a), 2(b), 2(d), and 2(e), respectively. Specifically, the average particle sizes of the Co₃O₄ and Co₂P/CoP are about 50 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: BF-STEM and EDS mapping show Co and P distributed throughout Co₂P/CoP nanoparticles with higher Co atomic content than P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM (BF-STEM) of Co₂P/CoP and corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping indicated the Co and P are distributed in the Co₂P/CoP sample, and the atomic content of Co is higher than P.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₂P/CoP shows interplanar lattice spacings of ≈0.231 nm (CoP (201)) and ≈0.271 nm (Co₂P (111)); pure CoP shows 0.189 nm (211), 0.247 nm (111); pure Co₂P shows 0.214 nm (220), 0.285 nm (120).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the inverse Fourier transform (IFFT), the interplanar lattice spacings could be obtained as ≈0.231 and ≈0.271 nm, corresponding to the orthorhombic CoP (201) and Co₂P (111) facets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Two sets of circular spots confirm polycrystalline phases of both CoP and Co₂P in heterostructure; single phases confirmed in pure CoP and Co₂P references.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figs. 3(a)–3(g), two sets of circular spots in SAED indicate polycrystalline phases of CoP and Co₂P existing in the heterostructure Co₂P/CoP sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Work functions measured as 3.82 eV for pure CoP and 4.43 eV for pure Co₂P, driving self-driven electron transfer from CoP to Co₂P in heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and Xray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed the effective promotion of the self-driven transferring of electrons from CoP to Co₂P... As a result, Co₂P has a work function of 4.43 eV, noticeably higher than that of CoP (3.82 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p Co-P peaks at 778.57, 793.47 eV positively shifted in Co₂P/CoP vs pure phases (Co more positive); P 2p peaks at 129.26, 130.18 eV negatively shifted (P more negative), confirming electron redistribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 778.57 and 793.47 eV belong to the Co-P bond... Notably, compared to pure Co₂P and CoP control samples, the binding energies of Co-P bond in Co₂P/CoP are positively shifted.

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl values: Co₂P/CoP-350 = 130.4 mF/cm² (highest), Co₂P/CoP-300 = 48.9 mF/cm², Co₂P/CoP-400 = 49.4 mF/cm², pure CoP = 12.5 mF/cm², pure Co₂P = 23.0 mF/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl results calculated by linear fitting in 1.24 V vs. RHE are shown in Fig. 4(d). Co₂P/CoP-350 possesses the largest C_dl (130.4 mF/cm²).

nodes.characterization_summary: R_ct = 0.336 Ω for Co₂P/CoP-350 (lowest), 3.117 Ω for CoP, 1.864 Ω for Co₂P; in situ EIS shows Volmer (mid-freq) and Heyrovsky (low-freq) steps.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The smallest charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of heterostructure Co₂P/CoP-350 sample (R_ct = 0.336 Ω) compared to that of pure phase of CoP (R_ct = 3.117 Ω) and Co₂P (R_ct = 1.864 Ω).
